codeReview.summary: The skel-fixture implementation fully satisfies VAL-SKEL-013 and the feature description. The exported BootDaemon function at internal/interfaces/tui/testfixture/ correctly boots foxctl web serve -p 0 with a temp FOXCTL_STORAGE_ROOT, discovers the OS-chosen port via lsof, seeds agents deterministically via direct SQLite store insertion, and registers t.Cleanup for teardown with sync.Once protection for fatal paths. All 18 test cases pass with race detection. Code is idiomatic Go with proper concurrency primitives.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The lsof-based port discovery uses exec.Command without exec.CommandContext. While the outer discoverListeningPort loop handles timeout via its own ctx, if the lsof command itself hangs (e.g., due to OS-level resource constraints), the cmd.Wait() in the goroutine would not be interruptible by the outer context. This is a minor edge case but worth documenting if the fixture is used in resource-constrained CI environments.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: testfixture.go:294-298 — lsofPort runs exec.Command with no context cancellation

sharedStateObservations.observation: The lsof port discovery on macOS is documented as macOS-specific in discoveredIssues. This should be tracked as a known constraint for Linux CI. The fix suggestion (using /proc/net/tcp or ss on Linux) is noted but not implemented. Future validators should be aware this may need addressing before the fixture works on Linux CI runners.

summary: The skel-fixture implementation passes scrutiny. It fulfills all VAL-SKEL-013 requirements: exported BootDaemon function at the correct path (internal/interfaces/tui/testfixture/), temp FOXCTL_STORAGE_ROOT with clean teardown, OS-chosen port via lsof, deterministic agent seeding returning IDs, sync.Once-protected cleanup on t.Cleanup including fatal paths, and no process/directory leaks. 18 test cases cover all surfaces including the cleanup verification subtests. The implementation is idiomatic Go with proper mutex-protected safeBuffer, bounded retry loops with context cancellation, and graceful then forced kill. Two minor non-blocking observations: lsof cmd lacks context cancellation (edge case), and the macOS-specific lsof behavior is documented as a known constraint for future Linux support.
